name: South Bridge and the River Nene

layers.essential_history: [[c:Oundle sits on the River Nene, which loops around the east and south of the town and forms the parish boundary on those sides.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:Close by is Barnwell Country Park: about 37 acres of lakes, riverbank and meadows with waymarked trails, flat paths and a café. A good place to extend your walk.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:By the river, Silas the mason admits he was here at midnight, checking the barges of stone. The boatman swears to it. (Long walk only: this clears Silas.)]]

evidence: [[c:Silas the mason was at the river checking barges at midnight. The boatman saw him.]]
directions_to_next: [[c:Head north-east, about 390 metres as the crow flies, to the Ship Inn. Head back up into the town to West Street. Keep to pavements and public paths.]]

puzzle.title: [[c:The boatman's tally]]
material: [[c:BOATMAN: "Silas counted my barges at midnight: seven barges, each with six blocks of stone."]]
puzzle.question: [[c:How many blocks of stone did Silas count?]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:Forty-two. Counting that many blocks took Silas most of the night, so he was at the river, not the Talbot.]]
puzzle.fallback: [[c:Stuck? Take a hint: hints are free.]]
